bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: State-level mining taxes (Supreme Court ruling empowers states; MOIL claims no past liability; future royalty/tax exposure in MP/Maharashtra remains a risk); Long lead times for EC approvals (12-24 months); Exploration success rate low (3/1000); Delay in JV finalization; Global manganese price volatility; Labor and environmental compliance pressures
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident, aggressive, and execution-focused; Repeated emphasis on 'best ever' metrics; Clear roadmap to 3.5M tons by 2030; Transparent on constraints (EC timelines, exploration uncertainty); Proactive on renewables and cost control; No hedging or price guidance beyond Q2; Tone suggests strong internal alignment and urgency
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: MOIL's 60% renewable energy usage (20MW wind + 10.5MW solar) is unmatched in Indian mining and reduces long-term cost volatility; EMD plant is India's only one — creates captive demand and premium pricing; 100+ year mine leases (up to 2042) are a rare, durable competitive moat in Indian mining; Public sector ownership (53% GoI) ensures policy support and lease security; Exploration success is converting resources to reserves at scale (7.98M tons added in FY24) — a hidden value driver
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Largest producer of manganese ore in India with a market share of about 49% and large reserves; total reserves and resources of 127.01 million MT of manganese ore.
- Holds the majority of the country's total demonstrated reserves of high/medium grade manganese ore.
- Only producer of Electrolytic Manganese Dioxide (EMD) in India, supplying the pharmaceutical, battery and chemical industries.
- Debt-free balance sheet with high net worth and strong cash reserves, giving capacity to fund large investment plans.
- Reserves sit in the Central Indian Manganese belt with deposits of generally regular shape, and mines are centrally located with strong customer ties.
- Logistical advantage — all mines are well connected to State/National Highways, and most sit on the South East Central Railway network with railway sidings.
- Qualified, technically skilled manpower with peaceful industrial relations; highest-ever manganese ore production of 19.07 lakh tonnes in FY 2025-26 with output per man shift up to 1.616 MT.
- Designated as State Trading Enterprise (STE) / canalizing agency for export of manganese ore from India, earning canalizing fees.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Cyclicality of, and single-sector dependence on, the steel industry — Manganese ore demand is linked to the steel industry, which is cyclical; management flags 'high dependency on only one sector i.e. steel industry', so any slowdown in steel demand, or over-supply from international markets at cheaper rates, directly hits volumes and realisations.
- Import price of manganese ore / global price deflation — Described as 'the biggest threat' — a decline in the import price of manganese ore erodes the company's profit margin, and international prices are largely dependent on Chinese demand and availability. FY26 profit decline was itself attributed to a fall in net sale realisation of about 6%.
- Single-product concentration — The company is largely a single-product company, so any adverse impact on the manganese ore industry hits profitability; the manufactured-product lines (electrolytic manganese dioxide and ferromanganese) are small in volume terms and are not a meaningful offset.
- Delay in mine leases, regulatory and environmental approvals — Delay in obtaining fresh mine leases delays commissioning of new mines and affects expansion/investment plans; management separately warns that any delay in regulatory approvals may impact long-term growth. Uncertain geomorphology also delays project execution.
- Mining safety hazards, deepening operations and labour intensity — Mining involves structural collapses, equipment accidents, exposure to dangerous substances and respiratory problems. The BRSR notes that ~70% of operations are underground, accounting for 65% of total production, and that deepening existing mines and sinking new vertical shafts may increase safety challenges. MOIL is also a labour-intensive organisation, so labour-related risk factors can materially affect production performance.
- Rising cost of production — Cost of production may rise with increasing depth of deposits, revision in wages of regular employees and revision in minimum wages for contractual employees; narrow ore bodies make full mechanisation relatively difficult.
- Regulatory compliance and environmental remediation cost — As a mining company MOIL faces extensive health, safety and environmental regulation; evolving standards and community expectations expose it to increased compliance cost and unforeseen environmental remedial expenses, with legal penalties and reputational harm on non-compliance.
- Environmental impact of mining and processing manganese ore — Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table: mining and processing can cause habitat destruction, soil erosion, water pollution and air contamination, with intensifying regulatory oversight.

business.body: MOIL is engaged in exploration, exploitation and marketing of various grades of manganese ore, operating ten mines (seven underground and three opencast) and two plants through 'Mine to Mill' operations. Alongside ore it makes value-added products — electrolytic manganese dioxide (EMD) and ferro manganese (including slag) — and generates electricity from its own wind turbine generators. Its customers are steel manufacturers, ferroalloy producers and processors that add value to MOIL's products, while EMD goes to the pharmaceutical, battery and chemical industries; the company does not export its own products but acts as the State Trading Enterprise / canalizing agency for export of manganese ore from India.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Strategic Management Plan-2030 (SMP-2030): almost double manganese ore production to 3.50 million tonnes by 2030 and retain market leadership.
- Develop and mechanise existing mines and sink new vertical shafts to sustain and enhance production from deeper levels — high-speed shafts at Balaghat and Gumgaon under implementation, with new shafts planned at Dongri Buzurg, Kandri and Chikla.
- Add new leases and convert Prospecting Leases to Mining Leases in already reserved manganese-ore-bearing areas, and explore manganese ore mines in different states of the country.
- Acquire mineral assets in and outside the country, backed by strategic alliances and off-take agreements with manganese ore producers abroad; consultants/advisors empanelled and proposals under examination.
- Form joint ventures with state mining corporations — the JV company with Madhya Pradesh State Mining Corporation Ltd was incorporated on 4th June 2026 after Ministry of Steel and DIPAM approvals; the MoU with Gujarat Mineral Development Corporation is suspended due to local issues.
- Beneficiate accumulated manganese ore dumps at the mines to augment supply of high grade ore, with beneficiation projects included in the FY 2026-27 capex plan.
- Value addition and diversification beyond ore — electrolytic manganese dioxide and ferro manganese, plus 'Mine to Mill' expertise supported by R&D and industry-academic collaboration.
- Operate the State Trading Enterprise (STE) mandate for export of manganese ore from India through an online e-bid platform and global tenders, and explore exporting MOIL's own ore grades.
- Maintain a debt-free balance sheet and deploy surplus funds under a Board-approved Investment Policy while sustaining dividends in line with DIPAM guidelines.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: MOIL, the largest manganese ore producer in India, plans to enhance production to 3.50 million MT by 2030 under a strategic management plan, and expansion is built around deepening and mechanising existing mines rather than greenfield capacity. Second vertical shafts have already been completed at the Chikla, Ukwa and Munsar mines. Two large-diameter high-speed vertical shafts are under implementation: 750 mtr depth (revised to 660 mtr) at Balaghat Mine and 330 mtr depth at Gumgaon Mine, conceptualised to raise Gumgaon from 1,50,000 MT to 3,50,000 MT and Balaghat to 8,00,000 MT. Both projects were delayed by the Covid pandemic, supply-chain disruption, heavy in-rush of water (particularly in the Balaghat shaft) and visa issues, which also pushed out the planned production enhancement; shaft sinking, lining and equipping are now complete, with the ore skip winder dry run, decking device, shaft fittings, civil foundations and surface transport system in progress at Balaghat, and roof supporting, OTC widening and collar concreting and the approach road in progress at Gumgaon. Upcoming shafts include a 505 mtr deep production shaft plus two ventilation shafts (250 mtr and 260 mtr) at Dongri Buzurg, a 425 mtr deep second vertical shaft at Kandri and a 408 mtr deep third vertical shaft at Chikla, all with cage and skip hoisting on friction winders; tendering is in progress. Capex plans also cover development of new mining leases and areas, regular additions/modifications/replacements of fixed assets, beneficiation projects and R&D. During FY 2025-26 environmental clearances were granted for the Chikla (150.65 Ha), Munsar (193.27 Ha) and Gumgaon (212.736 Ha) areas, adding 6,50,008 TPA and taking total EC capacity to 33,28,800 TPA as on 31 March 2026. Inorganic growth is being pursued through acquisition of mineral assets in and outside the country with off-take agreements and empanelled advisors, and through state JVs: the joint venture company with Madhya Pradesh State Mining Corporation Ltd was incorporated on 4th June 2026 after Ministry of Steel and DIPAM approvals, following core drilling that established ore bodies at the Bhudkum Block in Chhindwara and the Selva Block in Balaghat, while the October 2019 MoU with Gujarat Mineral Development Corporation is suspended due to local issues.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Manganese ore demand outlook is described as 'very positive' because of the huge gap between domestic demand and supply — FY26 domestic consumption was about 9 million tonnes against production of 3.85 million tonnes.
- Higher crude steel production and domestic alloy capacity expansion are named as the factors driving manganese ore demand; India's crude steel production rose 10.7% y-o-y in FY26 to 168.4 million tonnes and crude steel capacity rose to 220 million tonnes.
- India remains a net importer of manganese ore — imports rose about 5% y-o-y in FY26 to about 6.90 million tonnes — which management frames as an import-substitution opportunity for domestic producers.
- Management expects imported manganese ore prices might ease in the near term, which could boost import volumes into the country — a competitive headwind on realisations.
- The National Steel Policy 2017 roadmap (300 MnTPA steelmaking capacity and 158 kg per capita consumption by FY 2030-31) implies a manganese ore requirement of about 11 million tonnes.
- World Steel Association Short Range Outlook: global steel demand +0.3% in 2026 to 1,724 Mt and +2.2% in 2027 to 1,762 Mt; India projected to grow 7.4% in 2026 and 9.2% in 2027 as the world's fastest-growing major steel market, led by infrastructure-led construction and autos.
- Chinese steel demand contraction narrowing to -1.5% in 2026 and flat in 2027; international manganese ore prices are largely dependent on Chinese demand and availability, so China is the key swing factor for MOIL's realisations.
- Over 95% of world manganese production is used in steelmaking, so MOIL's demand is structurally tied to steel output rather than to any other end-use.
- Mix headwind flagged in FY26: EMD demand from the battery sector was not encouraging and ferro manganese sales fell on lower availability of quantity; profit decline was attributed to a fall in net sale realisation of about 6%.
- Resource base of 127.01 million MT of manganese ore, dominant position, medium-to-high grade reserves, centrally located mines and strong customer ties are cited as the reasons MOIL is positioned to capture India's steel demand growth.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: MOIL is India's dominant manganese ore producer with best-ever FY24 performance and aggressive expansion plans to capture 32% of India's projected 11M ton steel-grade manganese demand by 2030, backed by 100+ year mine leases, record exploration, and capex exceeding PAT. Its vertically integrated EMD plant and renewable energy leadership offer unique defensive growth in a critical steel input sector.
